newsitem.title: UK: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 13.
newsitem.headline: WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST - AUGUST 13.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

MUNICH - ISPR, which markets sports stars and is jointly owned by the Kirch Group and Axel Springer Verlag, says it signed a worldwide exclusive marketing rights deal with international soccer goalkeeper Andreas Koepke.

LONDON - Advertising agency DDB Needham says McDonalds Argentina has chosen Rainuzzo DDB in Argentina to handle its advertising account, beginning in September. Rainuzzo DDB said McDonald's will be its largest client, with significant growth potential.

CHICAGO - Euro RSCG Tatham, a unit of Euro RSCG Worldwide, has become one of the fastest-growing ad agencies in Chicago during the past 12 months. Tatham has added nearly $150 million in new business billings, including the estimated $90 million Red Lobster restaurant account, the single-largest account in the agency's 50-year history.

LONDON - Many advertising executives in Britain feel anxious and uncertain about business prospects, despite the fact the industry is growing at a healthy pace, a specialised accountancy firm says. Bob Willott, a partner at Willott Kington Smith, says too many agencies are chasing too few accounts.

FRANKFURT - German television broadcasters are premiering new programmes to around 3,000 marketing, product and advertising managers at the industry's first trade fair aimed at boosting sales of advertising space as market growth slows.

BEIJING - China's first commercial blimp operation has been set up by a Singapore company. The 39-metre helium airship, which can be rented for $12,000 a day, flies illuminated over the nation's capital with messages of which brand of beer to swill or mobile phone to dial.

LONDON - Advertising agency Ammirati Puris Lintas, Budapest, says its campaign to launch Danish beer Tuborg in Hungary will target an upmarket audience, carrying the theme "Tuborg surpasses everything".

MOUNTAIN VIEW, California - Netscape Communications Corp. says it will ship Netcaster, a software product for sending news and information through the Internet, later this week. Netscape signed agreements with 700 media and entertainment companies to distribute news, financial information and sport scores to customers' personal computers.

SYDNEY - Australia is well placed to be a world leader in the on-line industry and enjoy economic growth and job creation from the Internet, says Communications Minister Richard Alston at the Internet World '97 conference in Sydney. Employment in Australia's information technology industry will grow to 650,000 by the year 2000, from around 500,000 currently, Alston says.

PARIS - The audience share of French private television station TF1 slumped in July compared to June, while public channels France 2 and France 3 saw a strong rise in their audience in July from June, according to monthly figures from measurement institute Mediametrie.

MELBOURNE - Australian multi-media publisher PMP Communications Ltd says all its businesses are now trading above the same time last year, following a flat period in the first few weeks of the 1997/98 (July/June) year.

NEW YORK - General Electric Co unit NBC attracted the largest prime-time evening audience during the week of August 4 to August 10, Nielsen Media Research says. In second place was Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS.

FRANKFURT - Cable home shopping channel H.O.T. is now available to 365,000 households in the southwestern state of Baden-Wuerttemberg. In three weeks, another 180,000 cable customers in the state will be able to watch H.O.T., the station says.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

BEIJING - China sold 820,000 domestic brand personal computers in the first six months of 1997, up 94.2 percent from the year-ago period, the Market Daily says. The output value of China's PC industry reached 57 billion yuan ($6.9 billion) in January-June, the newspaper says, quoting figures from the Ministry of Electronics Industry.

SAN JOSE, Costa Rica - Demand in the United States and Europe for a new variety of pineapple will boost the Costa Rican pineapple trade's output to an expected $75 million this year. Pindeco, a division of Del Monte Fresh Produce, plans to develop 500 hectares of new plantations to grow the pineapple called "Del Monte Gold", and expects to boost production by 800,000 boxes each year for the next three years, an industry businessman says.

MAGADAN, Russia - Frank's Siberian Supreme, a four-man operation making American ice cream for a corner of the Russian Far East, has attracted the attention of the American government-funded U.S.-Russia Investment Fund, which is finalising a deal to buy 40 percent of Siberian Supreme for $300,000. Siberian Supreme officials plan to expand to other cities in the Russian Far East, and then into Siberia.

NEW YORK - Lucent Technologies Inc. says it will join with Compaq Computer Corp., Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp. to speed the convergence of personal computers and television sets, using digital technology. The four companies hope to develop affordably priced digital television products and services by the fall of 1998, Lucent says.

MANILA - Republic Resources and Development Co (Redeco) says it has signed an agreement with Hong Kong-based Lucky Seven Overseas Co to form a cigarette making company in the Philippines. Redeco will hold a 60 percent stake in the new venture while Lucky Seven would hold the remaining 40 percent, says Redeco president Sherwin Gatchalian.

TOKYO - Sony Corp says that it, Philips Electronics NV and Hewlett-Packard Co have applied to the European Computer Manufacturers Association for approval of a format for DVD-RAMs (digital video disc random-access memories).

WELLINGTON - New Zealand International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith hopes major exporters such as the Dairy Board will gain from lower tariffs on a range of products including cheese and milk negotiated in Beijing as part of China's accession to the World Trade Organisation.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

JERUSALEM - A Sabbath computer keyboard has been devised by Orthodox Jewish space scientists who needed to send a signal to their malfunctioning satellite on the Jewish Sabbath, when religious law forbids them to use electricity. The team is now working on electric wheelchairs for the Sabbath.

CHUAO, Venezuela - A handful of financiers are seeking to re-market the the Rolls Royce of chocolate: the Venezuelan cacao bean. Entrepreneurs hope to follow in the footsteps of local firms which have recently signed joint ventures with foreign chocolatiers, such as France's prestigious Valrhona, and restore the dented prestige of the bean.
